transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Let's get started. As you know, we've got the routine annual inspection on the 25-ton overhead crane in Bay 2 coming up this Friday. We've got eight finished frames already staged in the bay and four more expected during the week, so this inspection needs to be coordinated carefully to minimize disruption. Before I finalize any decisions on the work plan, I want to follow our standard pre-job huddle process — I need maintenance, production scheduling, and EHS to all review the plan. So let's hear from each of you: what do we need to consider for this inspection?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something before we go any further. During my inspection this morning, I found that the crane brake lining is at 18% remaining. Our maintenance standard requires immediate removal from service below 20%. This isn't something that can wait until Friday's annual inspection — the crane needs to come down now. It's a 6-hour brake replacement, and after that we need to do a 125% rated-capacity proof-load test before the crane can return to service. I haven't entered this in the maintenance system yet, but I'm doing so as soon as we wrap up here. Given the eight finished frames staged in Bay 2 and four more coming, we need to figure out how to handle those movements without the crane.

transcript.text: I need to share something from my EHS walkdown that directly affects how we handle this. The forklift route through Bay 2 crosses the active pedestrian aisle, so forklifts may not be used as a substitute for the overhead crane in that bay. Additionally, any crane work — including the proof-load test Jonas mentioned — requires a 10-meter exclusion zone and a designated spotter. I recorded this in my walkdown notes but have not yet issued the bay notice. Given that Jonas needs to pull the crane now and Priya has a hard Thursday 15:00 deadline for 8 frames, we need to figure out an alternative movement method that doesn't rely on forklifts in Bay 2, and we need to plan for the exclusion zone during the brake replacement and proof-load test.

commitments.detail: Enter the brake lining finding in the maintenance system immediately and begin the 6-hour brake replacement now. Crane is removed from service effective immediately per the below-20% standard.
Issue the Bay 2 notice now establishing a 10-meter exclusion zone around the crane work area and assigning a designated spotter for the duration of the brake replacement and proof-load test.

Work with Jonas and Elliot to identify an alternative lift method that is not a forklift in Bay 2 to move the 8 staged frames to shipping before Thursday 15:00. Options to evaluate include an outside mobile crane, a different bay's overhead crane with re-routing, or a subcontracted rigger. Report back with a feasible plan by end of today.
After the 6-hour brake replacement is complete, conduct the 125% rated-capacity proof-load test with exclusion zone and spotter in place before returning the crane to service.

The remaining 4 frames can stay in Bay 2 until Monday per the confirmed shipping schedule, and can be moved with the crane once it is returned to service after the brake replacement and proof-load test.
